title: Greywater Bay Rising Revisited
premise: True-crime podcaster Ada Coldharbour has spent years solving the deaths police dismissed, always from the shadows. When twin letters arrive—one confessing to her sister's drowning twenty years ago, one promising a second death in Greywater Bay—Ada is forced home, where the town that closed the case still wants it buried. As she unravels a conspiracy binding the bay's founding families, she falls for the detective assigned to stop her investigation, and both must choose between duty and truth. In the end Ada exposes the killer at the drowned chapel on Greywater Bay, but justice comes outside the law: the confession airs on her final episode, and she leaves town with the detective rather than the verdict.
about_author: Freya Joubert grew up in a fading coastal town where everyone knew which families could not be questioned, and never forgot it. She writes mysteries about small places with long memories and the people brave enough to dig.

chapters.title: The Twin Letters
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Two envelopes arrive the same morning: one confessing to a drowning, one promising 'the next one soon.' Ada's hands shake as she realizes the name in the confession is her sister. Emotional beat: dread cracking open a carefully controlled life.

chapters.title: Three Accidents
chapters.summary: POV Ada, flashback-structured. We learn how Ada quietly solved three 'accidental' deaths through her podcast, The Cold File, without ever going public. Emotional beat: pride shadowed by loneliness—she has never let anyone truly know her.

chapters.title: Greywater Bay
chapters.summary: POV Ada. She drives back to the fog-bound town she fled at nineteen, past shuttered cannery rows and the drowned chapel visible at low tide. Emotional beat: the sick recognition of a place that remembers you better than you remember it.

chapters.title: The Welcome Wagon
chapters.summary: POV Ada. At her aunt's boarding house, old neighbors offer casseroles and warnings in equal measure; someone has already keyed her car. Emotional beat: hostility wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Detective Rook
chapters.summary: POV Rook. Detective Elias Rook, newly transferred and assigned to watch the podcaster stirring the bay, meets Ada and recognizes a fellow outsider. Emotional beat: reluctant fascination—he was sent to stop her, not help her.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: POV Ada. At the tidal flats where her sister Maren drowned, Ada finds a rusted locket that should have been logged as evidence decades ago. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Founding Families
chapters.summary: POV Ada. She maps the town's power structure: the Harrow shipping fortune, the Vane family's marina empire, Judge Aldous Crane presiding over everything. Emotional beat: cold clarity about who benefits from a closed case.

chapters.title: First Interview
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Ada interviews elderly Ruth Vane, who nearly speaks before her son interrupts and ends the recording. Emotional beat: hope strangled mid-breath.

chapters.title: Threats, Politely Worded
chapters.summary: POV Ada. A lawyer's cease-and-desist arrives, then an anonymous note: 'Maren talked too. Look how that ended.' Emotional beat: fear she refuses to show anyone.

chapters.title: Coffee at the Edge of Town
chapters.summary: POV alternating Ada/Rook. Rook warns her off; Ada counters with evidence he can't ignore. They argue for two hours over bad coffee. Emotional beat: the first spark of trust between adversaries.

chapters.title: The Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: POV Ada. At low tide Ada explores the half-submerged chapel where Maren was last seen alive, finding fresh boot prints in the silt. Emotional beat: the past is not finished happening.

chapters.title: Ruth's Letter
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Ruth Vane mails Ada a partial letter hinting that Maren witnessed something at the chapel the night she died—a transaction, not an accident. Emotional beat: vindication laced with terror.

chapters.title: Second Death
chapters.summary: POV Rook. Cannery archivist Tom Pell, who'd contacted Ada about records, is found dead in his boat—an apparent heart attack. Emotional beat: the promise in the second letter, kept.

chapters.title: The Cold File Goes Loud
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Against her instincts, Ada publishes an episode naming Pell's death suspicious. Downloads explode; so do the threats. Emotional beat: invisibility traded for impact.

chapters.title: Rook's Dilemma
chapters.summary: POV Rook. His captain orders him to build a case against Ada for obstruction instead of investigating Pell. Emotional beat: duty grinding against conscience.

chapters.title: The Harrow Vault
chapters.summary: POV Ada. With Rook looking away, Ada breaks into the Harrow estate's records room and photographs ledgers showing payments to Judge Crane dated the week after Maren's death. Emotional beat: triumph curdling—the conspiracy is bigger than one murder.

chapters.title: Caught
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Marcus Harrow catches Ada leaving; Rook arrives and covers for her, burning his own credibility. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in shared risk.

chapters.title: Aunt Vera's Silence
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Her aunt finally admits she saw Maren leave the chapel with someone the night she died—and has been paid to stay quiet ever since. Emotional beat: betrayal inside the only safe harbor.

chapters.title: The Confession Letter, Again
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Forensic comparison shows the confession letter's paper matches stationery from the Greywater Yacht Club. Emotional beat: the killer is a member, comfortable, untouchable.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: POV Rook. A hurricane tracks toward the bay; the town battens down, and Rook realizes the killer will use the storm as cover. Emotional beat: racing the calendar.

chapters.title: Ruth Vane Dies
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Ruth is found dead hours before her follow-up interview—a fall down her stairs. Ada finds Ruth's completed letter hidden in a hymnal. Emotional beat: guilt like a stone in the chest.

chapters.title: The Full Letter
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Ruth's letter names what Maren saw: crates moving through the chapel tunnel at night—smuggling, sanctioned by the founding families, with Maren demanding a cut or exposure. Emotional beat: her sister was braver than anyone knew.

chapters.title: Suspects Narrow
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Ada and Rock cross-reference: who was young enough, present enough, strong enough? Three names remain—Marcus Harrow, Julian Vane, and Judge Crane's son. Emotional beat: the net tightening around people with infinite resources.

chapters.title: The Trap Baited
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Ada announces on-air that she possesses the full letter and will reveal everything Friday. Emotional beat: deliberate self-exposure as bait.

chapters.title: Rook Crosses the Line
chapters.summary: POV Rook. He copies case files for Ada, knowing it ends his career if discovered. Emotional beat: love arriving disguised as insubordination.

chapters.title: Night Visit
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Someone enters the boarding house while she sleeps, leaving the original confession letter on her pillow—signed this time, with a date: Friday, high tide. Emotional beat: being hunted in your own bed.

chapters.title: Vera Confesses More
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Under pressure, Aunt Vera reveals the signer's identity was common knowledge among the wives, never spoken: the confession is genuine, and the killer wants a witness now. Emotional beat: horror at why—this is a performance, an audience sought.

chapters.title: The Storm Arrives
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Hurricane landfall; power fails; roads flood. Rook defies orders to reach Ada. Emotional beat: the world reduced to wind, water, and two people running toward each other.

chapters.title: High Tide at the Chapel
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Lured by a text from Vera's stolen phone, Ada goes to the drowned chapel as the tide rises. Emotional beat: walking into the exact shape of her sister's last night.

chapters.title: The Killer Unmasked
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Julian Vane confesses fully: he killed Maren to protect the smuggling route, then killed Pell and Ruth as the letters promised—because he wanted Ada to solve it, to make someone finally see. Emotional beat: evil that craves acknowledgment.

chapters.title: Rising Water
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Julian seals the chapel door as the tide floods in; Rook breaks through the seaward window just as Ada goes under. Emotional beat: near-drowning, rescue, breath returned.

chapters.title: Julian Escapes
chapters.summary: POV Rook. In the chaos, Julian vanishes into the storm; the flood destroys physical evidence. Emotional beat: despair—truth without proof convicts no one.

chapters.title: The Verdict That Won't Come
chapters.summary: POV Ada. The judge recuses himself, the DA hesitates, the families close ranks. Julian walks free pending trial that will never be fair. Emotional beat: the law failing exactly as it always has.

chapters.title: The Last Episode
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Ada broadcasts the finale: Ruth's letter read aloud, the ledger pages, Julian's recorded confession from the chapel, captured on her running recorder. Emotional beat: justice delivered to millions of ears when courts refused it.

chapters.title: Consequences
chapters.summary: POV Rook. Rook turns in his badge alongside his report; the state opens a real investigation into Crane and Harrow. Emotional beat: ruin and relief in the same breath.

chapters.title: Julian's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Stripped of name and protection, Julian is found at the chapel at low tide—by his own hand, the tide coming in. Emotional beat: ambiguous mercy; the sea closes its own case.

chapters.title: Maren's Grave
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Ada finally visits her sister's grave and says the words out loud: I found you, I believe you, it wasn't your fault. Emotional beat: grief completing its arc into peace.

chapters.title: What Vera Told the Wives
chapters.summary: POV Ada. The town's women begin speaking, one by one, a generation of silence ending in kitchen-table testimony. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not inherited.

chapters.title: Leaving the Bay
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Ada and Rook pack her car together; the podcast will continue from anywhere, everywhere. Emotional beat: love chosen over duty, freely, twice over.

chapters.title: Greywater Bay Rising
chapters.summary: POV Ada, epilogue. Months later, from a rented room far away, Ada records the first episode of a new season: the founding families' trial begins Monday. The tide rises on Greywater Bay, and this time the whole world is watching. Emotional beat: hard-won hope, still vigilant.
